core_entities.name: Company
core_entities.description: The B2B client entity that subscribes to the service for its employees.

core_entities.name: User
core_entities.description: The anonymous end-user (employee) interacting with the application. Linked to a company but without any Personal Identifiable Information (PII).

core_entities.name: Conversation
core_entities.description: A complete interaction session between a User and the AI agent, including all messages and the final outcome.

core_entities.name: Therapist
core_entities.description: A registered mental health professional available for consultations. Their profile and availabilities are managed.

core_entities.name: Booking
core_entities.description: A record of an appointment made by a User with a Therapist, managed via an external API (cal.com).

core_entities.name: Resource
core_entities.description: A self-help tool within the library (e.g., meditation audio, breathing exercise guide, podcast).

core_entities.name: CrisisLog
core_entities.description: A specific event log created when a conversation is flagged for acute crisis, for security and audit purposes.

edge_cases.analysis: A user needs to provide PII (name, email) to book a session with a therapist, which conflicts with the platform's anonymity principle. The architecture must ensure that PII is passed directly to the external booking service (cal.com) and is never stored alongside the user's anonymous conversation history in our database.

The external AI model API (Mistral) could be slow or unavailable. The backend must implement timeouts, retries with exponential backoff, and a circuit-breaker pattern. The client application should display a user-friendly message during delays.
The booking API could be down. The 'Take an appointment' feature must be disabled gracefully, informing the user of the temporary issue and suggesting other resources in the meantime.

A booking might be cancelled or modified directly in the therapist's calendar (cal.com). A webhook system is necessary to receive real-time updates from cal.com and keep our local `bookings` table synchronized.

Users must be associated with their employer without revealing their identity. The proposed solution is a one-time company code for initial registration, which generates a persistent anonymous user UUID and a device-specific JWT for subsequent sessions.

The system handles sensitive health data, requiring hosting on HDS (Hébergeur de Données de Santé) certified servers. All data, especially conversation content, must be encrypted both in transit (TLS) and at rest (e.g., using Supabase's pgsodium extension).
API calls to the LLM (Mistral) can be expensive. Rate limiting must be implemented on a per-user basis to prevent abuse and manage operational costs.

conversation_messages.name: conversation_id
conversation_messages.constraints: NOT NULL, REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

api_endpoints.purpose: Register a new anonymous user using a company-provided code. Returns a JWT.
Starts a new conversation session for the authenticated user.
Retrieves the message history for a specific conversation.
Sends a user message to the AI. The server processes it with the Mistral API and returns the AI's response.
Lists all available self-help resources (meditations, exercises, podcasts), with filtering options.
Lists available therapists and their profiles.
Fetches available booking slots for a specific therapist by proxying a request to the cal.com API.
Creates a new appointment. This endpoint receives user PII and forwards it to the cal.com API to create the booking, then saves a non-PII reference in the local DB.
Retrieves the list of upcoming and past bookings for the authenticated user.
Retrieves the information for the direct human support hotline.
Webhook endpoint to receive booking status updates from cal.com (e.g., confirmed, cancelled).
